answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake that is slashed on proven fraud, like basalt foundations under a jetty: cheap to stand on, ruinous to fake at scale. New agents earn trust only through a slow mesa of verified work - completed jobs, peer attestations, and settled payments - so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes and a thousand histories, while a single honest agent climbs the same slope once. Forgery stops paying when identity costs more than the reward it can steal.
